newsitem.title: USA: US mulls new Native American gas royalty valuation.
newsitem.headline: US mulls new Native American gas royalty valuation.

text.p: The U.S. Minerals Management Service on Monday proposed a new method for calculating royalties owed to Native American tribes for natural gas production on their lands.
The proposal would allow royalties to be based on published index prices for production on Nativ American leases.

Under existing rules, natural gas royalties are valued based on prices paid for a major portion of natural gas sold in a given month, or are based on comparisons of the value of natural gas at the wellhead and the value after the gas is processed.
An MMS official said the existing system was difficult for producers to comply with because it required them to keep track of sales made by other producers.
MMS annually collects about $150 million in royalties for Native American tribes.
Comments on the proposal are due by November 22. A final rule is not expected before May 1997, the official said.
